claims.text: A high-thermal-conductivity interlayer between the substrate and the FeMnNiGeSi-type film will enhance interfacial heat removal.
Enhanced interfacial heat removal will accelerate heat extraction during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Faster heat extraction will narrow the magnetic hysteresis loop relative to films on conventional substrates.
Faster heat extraction will improve the magnetocaloric response relative to films on conventional substrates.
A thin Cu or diamond-like-carbon layer can serve as the proposed high-thermal-conductivity interlayer.
The interlayer will improve film/substrate thermal coupling.
Improved thermal coupling will reduce localized thermal gradients at microstructural boundaries.
Localized thermal gradients at microstructural boundaries mediate magnetic-domain dynamics.
Thermal lag produces inhomogeneous temperature fields during cyclic magnetic cooling.
Inhomogeneous temperature fields lead to greater hysteretic losses and poorer magnetocaloric performance.
More uniform thermal conditions make magnetic-domain reorientation more consistent.
More consistent magnetic-domain reorientation reduces hysteresis-loop width and enhances magnetocaloric efficiency.
The modified film should show a sharper magnetocaloric transition or increased effective entropy change.
Improved thermal management should permit faster magnetic-cooling cycle frequencies.
Baseline films on standard substrates are expected to have slower heat dissipation, broader hysteresis loops, and lower magnetocaloric efficiency because of thermal lag.
The predicted effect applies when dimensions are nanoscale, applied magnetic fields are low, and microstructural integrity remains similar to the as-deposited state.
Interlayer-related changes in adhesion or microstructure could influence the observed outcome.
